review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its definitions against Mathlib. The definitions are `ev`, `tw`, `pev`, `DD`, `restrictHom` and `restrictEquiv`. `ev`, `tw` and `pev` are named `eval₂Hom` specialisations. `pev` is rfl-equal to the project's own `NodeLocalized.pointEval`, but that is an in-project duplicate and not a Mathlib one, so I did not report it. The only finding is `restrictHom`, which re-implements the restriction of a ring map to a subring. I did not check how `restrictEquiv` is used. A replacement would have to deal with the coercion from `F.toSubring` to `↥F`, which I could not test. The many theorems (`add_pow_sub_pow_mem` and similar) were out of scope as standalone theorem duplication.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def restrictHom : ↥S →+* ↥S where
  toFun f := ⟨((σ ⟨(f : L₀), hSF f.2⟩ : ↥F) : L₀), hσS _ f.2⟩
findings.problem: `restrictHom` builds a ring homomorphism `S →+* S` by hand. It is the restriction of the ring map `σ` to the subring `S`, with domain `S` included into `F`. It spends four `Subtype.ext`/`change`/`rw ... ; rfl` proofs (`map_one'`, `map_mul'`, `map_zero'`, `map_add'`) to show that. Mathlib already has `RingHom.restrict` and `RingHom.codRestrict`, which restrict a ring map to subrings while preserving the coercion lemma `coe_restrict_apply`. It also has `Subring.inclusion`, which gives the inclusion `S →+* F.toSubring`. The file therefore carries its own competing restriction construction together with a custom `coe_restrictHom` lemma. It also needs a custom iterate lemma, `coe_restrictHom_iterate`.
findings.proposed_change: Define `restrictHom` as a composition of existing Mathlib maps. Take `(σ : ↥F →+* ↥F).comp (Subring.inclusion hSF)`, using the identification of `↥F.toSubring` with `↥F`. Then use `RingHom.codRestrict` (or `RingHom.restrict`) to land in `S`, with `hσS` supplying the membership proof. Keep the name `restrictHom` and the lemma `coe_restrictHom` (now closed by `rfl`), so downstream uses are unaffected. This removes the four hand-written field proofs.
findings.benefit: The file would reuse Mathlib's restriction machinery, so its simp lemmas and ring-hom structure come for free. The map's properties would no longer be proved by repeated `change`/`rw`/`rfl` coercion unfolding, and a reader would see at once that the map is the restriction of σ.
